Survey of the tools in 7 agent harnesses and 6 service benchmarks

items.title: Design review, round 1
done: Review received. Verdict: the scoring, clock and verifier-input specifications need a rewrite; the layered direction stands
All five blocking issues accepted
Six of our factual statements corrected; one reviewer statement rejected after checking the source
where: Reading notes with a stance on every item, kept with the project's internal files
checked: Every numeric counterexample in the review was recomputed by hand
The closest shopping benchmark was read in full, which showed our claimed gap there does not exist

items.title: Design revision after the review
plan: A scoring contract per task family, replacing the single normalised score
A state machine for scheduling, termination and what happens after a seat finishes
Trusted sealing of world state and event log before verification
Corrected rules: the 24-hour cancellation is the agency's own policy; California claim deadlines run from their real triggers

items.title: Interface definition v0.1
done: 2 roles and 3 seats: one booking agent, two travellers
30 actions: 25 visible to the agent, 19 to a traveller
23 entities, named after the fields of Duffel, Amadeus and Expedia where those exist
Authorization object: single-use, bound to a digest of what was consented to, with a charge ceiling
Typed message attachments: object references, fact requests and facts over 11 declared fact keys
33 error codes, and a world-time cost on every call so that repeated reads cannot freeze a deadline
13 worked examples that follow one booking from question to ticket
where: src/macbench/kernel/interface.py, the part other scenarios reuse
Ticketing page of this site: every action with its form, schema and example
checked: Tests cover: the export is complete, travellers cannot transact, the agent cannot consent, every action that moves money requires an authorization, money is integer cents everywhere, every example validates against the interface
open: Nothing runs yet. Every action has the status 'declared'
Round trips are modelled as two slices, but the first world will hold one-way trips only
The role-card format and the scoring contract are separate items

items.title: World data: airports, schedule, fares, inventory
done: 16 airports with real coordinates and time zones, 107 city pairs, 4 fictional carriers with hubs
One week of flights, 8 to 14 March 2027: 6,123 flights, 902 on a weekday, fewer on Saturday
Block times from distance and heading, so westbound takes longer than eastbound
Three fare brands and six fare classes per flight, with seats already sold; a party is priced from one class, so several seats can cost more each
Taxes, bag fees and seat fees in integer cents
Seat maps for three aircraft types; the taken seats equal the seats sold
Search as a pure function: nonstops and same-carrier connections that respect each airport's minimum connection time
Details a traveller would notice: red-eyes that land the next day, the clock change on 14 March, Phoenix without daylight saving, perimeter rules at LaGuardia and Washington National
where: src/macbench/domains/ticketing/world.py and search.py; every constant of the fare and load model is in one place at the top of world.py
tools/export_world.py writes the file this site displays
Ticketing page, World section: search results, departures, network, fares and rules
checked: 18 new automated tests, 38 in total, all pass

Tests cover: same seed gives the same world, schedule invariants on all 6,123 flights, great-circle distances against known values, time zones on the clock-change day, perimeter rules, fare ordering and the tax formula, connection rules, filters and sorting, error codes, seat maps against inventory
open: Loads and fares follow stated formulas with hand-set constants. They are not yet calibrated against public statistics
Search runs in Python. The site shows stored results for 12 sample searches, not live search
No delays or cancellations yet. Round trips are still out
